newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-KEY ELEMENTS OF WEDNESDAY'S CHAMPIONS' LEAGUE MATCHES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KEY ELEMENTS OF WEDNESDAY'S CHAMPIONS' LEAGUE MATCHES.

text.p: Analysis of key elements in Wednesday's European Champions' League matches:
Group A
Glasgow Rangers (Scotland) v Ajax Amsterdam (Netherlands)

England striker Paul Gascoigne, who scored a hat-trick against Motherwell on Saturday, is suspended along with Alex Cleland, Richard Gough and Craig Moore and Rangers, beaten 4-1 in Amsterdam, will struggle to find their first Champions' League points of the campaign.

Ajax appear to be on the mend after a dismal start to the season. Striker Patrick Kluivert is back from a serious knee injury and scored in his side's 4-1 victory over Roda. But wingers Tijani Babangida and Marc Overmars are doubtful while Jari Litmanen, Danny Blind, Winston Bogarde and Frank de Boer are not match fit.
Grasshopper Zurich (Switzerland) v Auxerre (France)

Grasshopper are returning to full strength and have scored 13 times in their last three league games. Key striker Kubilay Turkyilmaz has shaken off a nagging calf injury and should be joined by Nestor Subiat, who is fit again after tearing an Achilles tendon eight months ago. Murat Yakin aggravated a knee injury on Saturday but is expected to play. Switzerland's most capped international Alain Geiger is out with a groin injury.

Auxerre, level on points with their opponents, will be without Thomas Deniaud who scored three goals in their last two European ties. Deniaud hurt his ankle after scoring in his side's 7-0 thrashing of Lyon on Friday. Captain Sabri Lamouchi is doubtful with a knee injury.
Group B
Widzew Lodz (Poland) v Steaua Bucharest (Romania)
Widzew, looking for their first Champions' League points, are at almost full strength. Striker Rafal Siadaczka is the only absentee but they welcome back playmaker Ryszard Czerwiec after injury.

Steaua have a major headache at the back with sweeper Marius Baciu suspended and injured central defender Daniel Prodan doubtful. Attacking midfielder Adrian Ilie, who moves to Galatasaray later this year, plays in the Champions' League for the first time this season after being suspended for the first three matches. Steaua's only points came courtesy of Widzew, whom they beat 1-0 in Bucharest.
Borussia Dortmund (Germany) v Atletico Madrid (Spain)

Dortmund, virtually assured of a place in the quarter-finals after three straight victories, are nevertheless crippled by injury. Seven players are out injured and another two -- Juergen Kohler and Joerg Heinrich -- are suspended. But the Germans thrashed Arminia Bielefeld 5-0 at the weekend.

Atletico hope to have key midfielder Jose Luis Caminero back after a month-long injury but Argentine striker Diego Simeone is suspended. After two wins in their first two European matches Atletico lost at home to Dortmund and have looked fragile in the league. But they won away at the weekend after three successive defeats and are well placed to join Dortmund in the next round.
Group C
Juventus (Italy) v Rapid Vienna (Austria)

Alessandro Del Piero could replace either Frenchman Zinedine Zidane or Angelo Di Livio up front as the defending champions look to clinch their last-eight place. Croat Alen Boksic will lead Juve's attack. The Italians were held 1-1 at Roma at the weekend but were still technically and tactically brilliant.

Rapid warmed up for Europe by beating Sturm Graz 3-1 to go top in Austria, but they will be without Polish midfielder Andzrej Lesiak, scorer against the Italians in Turin. He had surgery on a knee injury this week.
Manchester United (England) v Fenerbahce (Turkey)

United defender Gary Pallister and midfielder Nicky Butt both have knee injuries and are regarded as "very doubtful". Norway's Ronny Johnsen, recovered from an Achilles tendon injury, is expected to replace Pallister. Ryan Giggs, who missed his side's 2-0 win in Istanbul, is still out of action. United have lost their last two league games 5-0 and 6-3 but are protecting a 40-year unbeaten home record in Europe.

The Turks arrived in Manchester with a squad of 20 players, several of whom face late fitness tests after a bruising 1-0 win against Trabzonspor. Danish defender Jes Hogh, Bulgarian forward Emil Kostadinov and Turkish midfielder Bulent Uygun all have groin injuries.
Group D
AC Milan (Italy) v Gothenburg (Sweden)

Milan enter this vital game in a state of shock and sorely in need of a win. Their weekend defeat at Fiorentina was their sixth of the season in all competitions and the pressure in the San Siro will be intense. Roberto Baggio, who played only 45 minutes against Fiorentina, may be dropped to make way for a midfield quartet picked from Dutchman Edgar Davids, Croat Zvonimir Boban, Massimo Ambrosini, Stefano Eranio and Tomas Locatelli. Midfielder Demetrio Albertini, Yugoslav Dejan Savicevic and captain Franco Baresi are doubtful through injury.

Gothenburg look to celebrate their recent Swedish league title by repeating their victory over Milan two weeks ago. They were given a psychological boost at the weekend when midfielder Jesper Blomqvist renewed his contract for a further year aftrer being linked to a number of foreign sides.
Porto (Portugal) v Rosenborg (Norway)

Porto, needing a single point to qualify for the next round, are injury-free and on form. Serbian winger Ljumbiko Drulovic set up four goals in their 5-0 win at the weekend. He and Brazilian Mario Jardel will again be key. Porto's other Brazilian forward Artur Oliveira and defender Sergio Conceicao, who have both been injured, should be fit by Wednesday.

Rosenborg striker Jahn Ivar "Mini" Jakobsen is out after being sent off in Trondheim a fortnight ago. Doubts persists about injured right-back Karl-Petter Loeken (leg muscle injury). Captain Bent Skammerlsrud may also miss out -- he is reluctant to leave home as his partner is expected to give birth at any moment.
